New Year 2027 Countdown by Country

New Year doesn't arrive everywhere at once. From the first stroke of midnight in Kiribati to the last one in American Samoa, the celebration takes about 25 hours to travel around the inhabited world. This page lists every country by the moment it enters 2027.

Which country celebrates New Year first?

The Line Islands of Kiribati, including Kiritimati (Christmas Island), are the first inhabited places to welcome the new year, at UTC+14:00 — that is 10:00 UTC on December 31. Samoa, Tonga and New Zealand's Chatham Islands follow shortly after, and Auckland is the first major city to celebrate.

The last inhabited places are American Samoa and Niue (UTC-11:00), which reach midnight at 11:00 UTC on January 1. The uninhabited Baker and Howland Islands (UTC-12:00) are technically the very last.

Why daylight saving time changes the order

On December 31 it is summer in the Southern Hemisphere, so places such as Sydney, Auckland and Santiago de Chile are on daylight saving time and celebrate one hour earlier than their standard offset suggests. The times on this page already include those changes.

Times are calculated for January 1, 2027. The "Your local time" column converts each moment to the time zone of your device.

Frequently asked questions

Which country celebrates New Year 2027 first?

Kiribati. Its Line Islands, including Kiritimati, use UTC+14:00 and reach midnight at 10:00 UTC on December 31 2026.

Which country celebrates New Year last?

Among inhabited places, American Samoa and Niue are last, at UTC-11:00 (11:00 UTC on January 1 2027). The uninhabited Baker and Howland Islands, at UTC-12:00, are the very last.

How long does it take for New Year to reach the whole world?

About 26 hours from the first time zone (UTC+14:00) to the last one (UTC-12:00), or about 25 hours counting only inhabited places.
